st.3: It had a burnt-brick fortification.
st.1: Its ploughed field shows furrows in one direction only, for a single crop.

x: None of the statements is correct. The ploughed field shows criss-cross furrows, suggesting two crops grown together; the fire altars belong to the Harappan level, not the pre-Harappan; the fortification was of mud bricks.

st.2: A bronze dancing girl
st.1: The steatite 'priest-king' bust

x: Only 4 is correct: Lothal has yielded a Persian Gulf (button) seal. The bronze dancing girl and the priest-king bust come from Mohenjo-daro; the Great Granary is at Harappa/Mohenjo-daro, not Lothal (Lothal has the ship seal, terracotta ship and copper dog).

st.4: Chetaka, chief of the Lichchhavis, was his maternal uncle, and Chetaka's daughter Chellana married Ajatashatru.
st.3: His mother Trishala was a Koliya princess.
st.1: He was born at Lumbini near Kapilavastu.

x: None of the statements is correct. Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali (Lumbini is the Buddha's birthplace); his father Siddhartha headed the Jnatrika clan, not the Shakyas; Trishala was a Lichchhavi princess; Chellana married Bimbisara and was Ajatashatru's mother.

st.3: Sona and Uttara were sent to the Yavana country.
st.2: Mahinda carried a branch of the Bodhi tree to Sri Lanka.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Sona and Uttara went to Suvarnabhumi (Maharakkhita went to the Yavana country); it was Sanghamitta, not Mahinda, who carried the Bodhi branch to Sri Lanka.

st.1: Gudimallam in Kurnool district has the earliest known Shiva linga.
st.3: Tantrism, which excluded women and Shudras, spread from the fifth century.

x: Only 4 is correct: the Kalamukha and Pashupata sects flourished under the Kakatiyas. Gudimallam is in Tirupati (old Chittoor) district; the ekamukhalinga bears one face, not four; Tantrism was open to women and Shudras.

st.3: Taniyur was a very large village administered as a single, separate unit.

x: All three statements are correct: Brahmadeya was rent-free land for Brahmins, Vellanvagai the land of non-Brahmin peasants, and a Taniyur a very large village (brahmadeya or nagaram) administered as a separate unit.

st.3: His canal from the Ganga to Hisar was about 150 miles long.
st.1: He built the largest network of canals among the Delhi Sultans but levied no tax on canal water.

x: Only 4 is correct: the Rajabwah was restored under Akbar as the Shihab Canal. Firoz levied the irrigation cess haq-i-sharb, at one-tenth (not one-fifth) of the produce; his 150-mile canal ran from the Yamuna to Hisar.

st.1: Timur, born at Kesh in 1336, claimed descent from Mahmud of Ghazni.
st.4: After it the Tughlaq state was replaced directly by the Lodi dynasty.
st.2: He crossed the Indus in September 1398 and sacked Delhi for three days during the reign of Ibrahim Lodi.

x: None of the statements is correct. Timur claimed descent from Chengiz Khan; he sacked Delhi in December 1398 under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq; the Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in 1526, not as an effect of the invasion; after Timur the Sayyids (1414) followed and regional kingdoms broke away.

st.1: He was born in Turkistan and sold to the Qazi of Nishapur before passing to Mahmud of Ghazni.

x: Only 2 is correct: Aibak was called Quran Khwan. He passed from the Qazi of Nishapur to Muhammad Ghori, not Mahmud of Ghazni; he died after a fall while playing chaugan (polo) at Lahore, not fighting the Khokhars.

st.1: Tansen is credited with the qaul and tarana forms and the raga Aiman (Yaman).

x: Only 3 is correct: the tabla is traditionally credited to Amir Khusrau. The qaul, tarana and raga Aiman are credited to Amir Khusrau, not Tansen; it was the Chishti, not the Suhrawardi, khanqahs that popularised sama.

st.1: Rohtas Fort near Jhelum was begun in 1541 under the supervision of Hemu.
st.4: Sher Shah's Tomb at Sasaram became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

x: Only 2 is correct: Rohtas Fort became a World Heritage Site in 1997. It was built under Todar Mal, not Hemu; the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built in 1541; Humayun's Tomb (not the Sasaram tomb) became a World Heritage Site in 1993.

st.1: The Dahsala was introduced in 1580 by Raja Man Singh.
st.3: Under the zabti, the dasturs were rates in kind (grain) per crop per bigha.
st.2: The Dahsala used the produce and prices of the single year 1580 only.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Dahsala (1580) was the work of Raja Todar Mal; it used the average produce and prices of the ten years 1571-80; the dasturs were cash rates; assessment by ploughs was used in parts of the Deccan, while nasaq prevailed in Bengal.

st.3: The Panch Mahal, a five-storeyed, entirely columnar pavilion in the style of a Buddhist vihara, stands in Agra Fort.
st.1: Fatehpur Sikri, built mainly of white marble, served as Akbar's capital from 1571 to 1585.

x: None of the statements is correct. Fatehpur Sikri is built mainly of red sandstone; the Buland Darwaza commemorates the victory over Gujarat, not Bengal; the Panch Mahal is at Fatehpur Sikri, not Agra Fort.

st.2: After Nizam-ul-Mulk's death (1748) he exploited the Mysore and Carnatic succession disputes.
st.1: He first used trained Indian sepoys, a method the English never adopted.

x: Only 4 is correct: Dupleix received a jagir at Valapadu. The English later copied his use of trained sepoys; he exploited the Hyderabad and Carnatic (not Mysore) disputes; he was made Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna, not the Godavari.

st.2: Sir Syed did not regard the absence of Indians in the Legislative Council as a cause of the revolt.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Sir Syed did name the absence of any Indian in the Legislative Council as a cause; P.E. Roberts called the revolt just a sepoy mutiny, not a national war of independence.

st.3: The Company agreed to pay the emperor Rs 26 lakh a year.

x: All three statements are correct: Shah Alam II granted the Diwani in 1765 when Clive was Governor of Bengal, and the Company agreed to pay him Rs 26 lakh a year (Rs 50 lakh was Awadh's war indemnity).

st.3: Under Wilkinson's Rule (1837) the Santhal Parganas were governed through Munda-Manki chiefs.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Indian Forest Act, 1878 made forests state property. The Paikas lost their lands after the British conquest of Odisha in 1803 (their revolt was in 1817); Wilkinson's Rule applied to the Kolhan, not the Santhal Parganas.

st.3: The grant was made available immediately from 1813.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Charter Act of 1813 set aside Rs 1 lakh a year for education. The General Committee of Public Instruction was set up in 1823, not 1835; the grant was not actually made available till 1823.

st.2: Maulana Mohammad Ali's Al-Hilal was banned in 1914.
st.4: Justice (1917) was edited by E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar).
st.1: Bande Mataram (1906), an English paper of Bombay, was associated with Aurobindo Ghosh and Bipin Chandra Pal.

x: None of the statements is correct. Bande Mataram was a Calcutta paper; Al-Hilal was Abul Kalam Azad's (Mohammad Ali ran Comrade); Qaumi Awaz was started in 1945, not 1935; Justice was edited by T.M. Nair.

st.2: The RSS was founded at Nagpur in 1925 by K.B. Hedgewar.

x: All three statements are correct: the CPI and CPI(M) date the party from Kanpur (1925) and Tashkent (1920) respectively, the RSS was founded at Nagpur in 1925 by K.B. Hedgewar, and Hasrat Mohani and Swami Kumarananda moved the complete-independence demand at Ahmedabad in 1921.

st.4: The NWFP ministry was headed by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. In Bombay the Congress fell just short of an absolute majority (85 of 175) yet formed the ministry; the NWFP ministry was headed by Dr Khan Sahib, not his brother Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

st.1: It ended separate electorates and introduced joint electorates for all communities.
st.2: It introduced universal adult franchise.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Act separated Sind from Bombay and split Bihar and Orissa. It extended separate electorates to the depressed classes, women and labour; it gave the vote to only about 14 per cent of the population; Burma was separated from India.

st.3: He was a priest of the Kali temple at Kalighat.
st.4: His guru in Vedanta was Bhairavi Brahmani.

x: Only 2 is correct: his original name was Gadadhar Chattopadhyay. 'My Master' was written by Vivekananda; he was a priest at Dakshineswar, not Kalighat; his Vedanta guru was Totapuri (Bhairavi Brahmani taught him Tantra).

st.1: Lal Mohan Ghose was the first Indian elected to the British House of Commons.

x: Only 3 is correct: Dadabhai Naoroji served on the Welby Commission. Lal Mohan Ghose only contested (1885) and lost - Naoroji was the first Indian elected; Naoroji won Central Finsbury in 1892 as a Liberal, not a Conservative.

st.3: The partition was first proposed in December 1903.

x: All three statements are correct: administrative convenience was the official reason, weakening Bengali nationalism and dividing Hindus and Muslims the real motive, and the partition was first proposed in December 1903.

st.1: In his sedition trial of 1897 Tilak got 18 months, and Annie Besant pleaded for him.
st.3: Tilak was released from the Cellular Jail, Andaman, in June 1914.

x: Only 2 is correct: in 1908 Tilak got six years in Mandalay. In 1897 it was Max Muller who pleaded for him; he was released from Mandalay, not the Andamans, in June 1914; Tilak's league (April 1916) had Joseph Baptista as president - Besant led her own league.

st.2: Darsi Chenchaiah was the founder-president of the Ghadar Party.
st.3: Darsi Chenchaiah's autobiography is Naa Jeevitha Yatra.
st.1: Darsi Chenchaiah belonged to Machilipatnam.

x: None of the statements is correct. Darsi Chenchaiah belonged to Kanigiri; he was the only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party, whose founder-president was Sohan Singh Bhakna; his autobiography is Nenu Naa Desam (Naa Jeevitha Yatra is Prakasam's); it was Sohan Singh Bhakna, not Har Dayal, who attended the Palasa Kisan Sabha.

st.3: The Montagu Declaration came before the Lucknow Pact.
st.1: The Komagata Maru incident came after Gandhi's return from South Africa.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Komagata Maru incident (1914) preceded Gandhi's return (January 1915); Tilak's League (April 1916) was founded before Besant's (September 1916); the Montagu Declaration (August 1917) came after the Lucknow Pact (December 1916).

st.3: Champaran, Kheda and the Pabna revolt belong to the Gandhian satyagraha phase of peasant movements.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Sanyasi Revolt followed the Bengal famine of 1770. The Permanent Settlement made zamindars the proprietors and cultivators their tenants; the Pabna revolt (1873) belongs to the pre-Gandhian phase.

st.1: It demanded that Muslim-majority areas be grouped as autonomous provinces within an Indian federation.
st.4: In reply, C. Rajagopalachari demanded Dravidistan at the Erode Conference in 1940.

x: Only 3 is correct: the League first observed Pakistan Day on 23 March 1943. The resolution demanded independent states for the Muslim-majority areas; the word 'Pakistan' was not used in it; the Dravidistan demand came from Periyar, not Rajaji.

st.2: The United Congress that won 119 seats in the mid-term poll was made up of the Congress, the Krishikar Lok Party and the Praja Socialist Party.

x: All three statements are correct: Prakasam's ministry fell on 15 November 1954 over prohibition, President's rule lasted till 28 March 1955, and the United Congress (Congress, Krishikar Lok Party and PSP) won 119 seats.

st.1: Kamaraj, like Rajaji before him, refused to share Madras city with the Andhras.

x: All three statements are correct: Rajaji and later Kamaraj refused any sharing of Madras, the Raja of Panagal proposed the Cooum as the boundary, and the Andhra Congress claimed half of the town.

st.3: Black-and-red ware is absent only at Visakhapatnam.

x: All three statements are correct: the Iron Age megaliths are called Rakshasa Gullu (Kurambara Gullu in Chittoor, Morivara Gullu in Anantapur), and black-and-red ware is absent only at Visakhapatnam.

st.3: Rajuvula and Sodasa ruled the Shaka branch at Ujjain.
st.2: Patika, known from the Taxila copper plate, belonged to the Western Kshatrapa branch in Saurashtra.

x: Only 1 is correct: Maues (Moga) was the first Shaka king. Patika belonged to the north-western branch at Taxila; Rajuvula and Sodasa ruled at Mathura, not Ujjain; it was Chandragupta II, not Samudragupta, who defeated Rudrasimha III.

st.1: Hala's Gathasaptasati calls them Andhras or Andhrabhrityas, i.e. servants or feudatories of the Andhras.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Satavahanas began as Mauryan feudatories. It is the Puranas, not the Gathasaptasati, that call them Andhras or Andhrabhrityas; the Andhras are listed in Ashoka's 13th, not 2nd, Rock Edict.

st.3: Dakshinapatheshwara was a title of Vasishthiputra Pulumavi.

x: All three statements are correct: Ekabrahmana and Varnasankarya-nirodhaka were Gautamiputra Satakarni's titles, Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana refers to horses that drank the three oceans, and Dakshinapatheshwara was Vasishthiputra Pulumavi's title (Satakarni I was Dakshinapathapati).

st.1: Kotilingala, claimed as an early political centre, is in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh.

x: Neither statement is correct. Kotilingala is in Karimnagar, Telangana; Pratishthana (Paithan) stood on the Godavari, not the Krishna.

st.2: Gautami Balasri funded the cave-vihara at Nasik.

x: All three statements are correct: titles like Mahasenapatni and Mahabhojaki came from husbands, Gautami Balasri funded the Nasik cave-vihara (she was not a Gathasaptasati poet), and kings used matronymics such as Gautamiputra.

st.2: It used the blue-grey schist of the north-west for its Tirthankara and Yaksha figures.
st.1: It produced Buddhist images only and no icons of Shiva, Vishnu or Surya.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Mathura Buddha has a decorated halo and clinging drapery. Mathura produced some of the earliest Shiva, Vishnu and Surya icons; it worked in spotted red sandstone (blue-grey schist is Gandhara's); it flourished under the Kushanas, not the Mauryas.

st.1: The interim Andhra Pradesh Secretariat and Legislature stand at Mangalagiri in Guntur district.

x: Neither statement is correct. The interim Secretariat and Legislature stand at Velagapudi in Thullur mandal; the Legislature building was inaugurated on 2 March 2017, not 2016.

st.2: The division of museum antiques under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 remains unfinished.

x: All three statements are correct: many Amaravati relics went to London and Madras museums, the division of museum antiques under the 2014 Act remains unfinished, and International Museum Day is on 18 May.

st.3: He was not the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty, which was founded by Indravarma.

x: All three statements are correct: Govinda Varma I expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region and bore the title Shadabhigna, and the dynasty was founded by Indravarma, not by him.

st.2: The Reddi chief Ambadeva was made head of Kadapa in 1272.
st.3: Rudrama Devi was killed in 1289 fighting the Ganga king Narasimhadeva, along with her general Mallikarjuna Nayaka.

x: Only 1 is correct: Narasimhadeva took Vengi in 1262 and the Kakatiyas regained it in 1278. Ambadeva was a Kayastha, not a Reddi; Rudrama Devi died fighting Ambadeva, not the Gangas; her death is recorded in the Chandupatla inscription, not at Tripurantakam.

st.1: The Reddi kings patronised Pashupata Shaivism, while Veerashaivism was the popular religion.

x: All three statements are correct: the Reddi kings patronised Pashupata Shaivism while Veerashaivism was popular, the Ghoderayas spread Shaivism from Tripurantakam, and Kumaragiri and Kataya Vema patronised Vaishnavism (Vadagalai matha at Ahobilam).

st.1: Bidar was the capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.
st.2: Amir Ali Barid founded the Adil Shahi dynasty.

x: Neither statement is correct. Golconda was the Qutb Shahi capital (Bidar was the Barid Shahi capital); the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur was founded by Yusuf Adil Shah, while Amir Ali Barid belongs to the Barid Shahis.

st.3: Vira Narasimha, son of Saluva Narasimha, was crowned in 1505 after killing Immadi Narasimha.
st.1: The Sangama was the longest-ruling dynasty; its last king Praudha Raya was removed in 1485 by Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.

x: None of the statements is correct. Praudha Raya was removed by Saluva Narasimha; Achyutaraya was a Tuluva, not an Aravidu; Vira Narasimha was the son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka.

st.3: The Kakatiyas were Shudras who rose through military service.

x: All three statements are correct: Veerashaivism gave rise to the Lingayats, Balijas and Jangamas, Vaishnavism to the Satanis and Dasaris, and the Kakatiyas were Shudras who rose through military service.

st.4: The Permanent (zamindari) Settlement followed their suppression.
st.1: The Nawab of Arcot ceded Kadapa, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary to the Company in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance.

x: Only 2 is correct: about 80 palegars resisted Thomas Munro. The Ceded Districts were ceded by the Nizam, not the Nawab of Arcot; the action lasted about 18 months, not six; the Ryotwari, not the Permanent Settlement, followed.

st.1: Nyapathi Subbarao held the title 'Gokhale of South India'.

x: Only 3 is correct: after 1908 Konda Venkatappayya and B.N. Sarma came to the fore. Nyapathi Subbarao's titles were Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda - 'Gokhale of South India' was Mocherla Ramachandra Rao, while 'Father of South India' was G. Subramania Iyer.

st.1: The Abolition Act received the assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1948 Act received the assent of Governor-General C. Rajagopalachari (2 April 1949), the Prakasam Committee held that the land belongs to the tiller, and Kala Venkata Rao introduced the Bill on 11 November 1947.

st.1: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was written not by him but by Viswanatha Satyanarayana.

x: All three statements are correct: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu is Viswanatha Satyanarayana's, and Garimella, born in 1893 at Gonedapadu, was jailed for a year from 9 February 1922 for 'Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu'.

st.1: The All India Progressive Writers' Association was founded at Lucknow in 1936 with Muhammad Iqbal presiding.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. The AIPWA's founding session (Lucknow, 1936) was presided over by Premchand, not Iqbal; Arasam's first conference was held at Tenali, not Vijayawada.

st.2: Komarraju founded the Rajaraja Narendra Andhra Bhasha Nilayam at Secunderabad in 1904.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The Rajaraja Narendra Andhra Bhasha Nilayam (1904) was at Hanamkonda, not Secunderabad; the Andhra Saraswati Parishad was set up at Hyderabad, not Warangal.

st.2: The Sungas were Brahmins.

x: All three statements are correct: the Harshacharita records Pushyamitra killing Brihadratha at an army review, the Sungas were Brahmins, and their heartland was Magadha, Malwa-Vidisha and the Narmada valley.

st.2: Al-Masudi visited the kingdom in the reign of Indra III.

x: All three statements are correct: Sulaiman ranked the Rashtrakuta king among the four great kings, Al-Masudi visited c. 915-16 under Indra III, and Balhara is the Arabic form of Vallabha.

st.2: He served as Shrikaranadhipa under Mahadeva and Ramachandra.

x: All three statements are correct: Hemadri wrote the Chaturvarga Chintamani, served as Shrikaranadhipa under Mahadeva and Ramachandra, and recorded that Jaitugi killed the Kakatiya Rudra.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh, with about 4.09% of India's population (2025-26), is the fifth most populous State.
st.1: As per Census 2011, cultivators still outnumbered agricultural labourers.

x: Only 2 is correct: the work participation rate in 2011 was 39.8%. In 2011 agricultural labourers outnumbered cultivators for the first time; Himachal Pradesh, not Punjab, had the highest Hindu share; Andhra Pradesh ranks tenth, not fifth.

st.3: The National Commission on Population (May 2000) is chaired by the Prime Minister.

x: All three statements are correct: India launched the first national family planning programme in 1952, adopted the target-free approach in April 1996 after Cairo, and the National Commission on Population is chaired by the Prime Minister.

st.4: She held that kinship had little bearing on Indian social organisation.
st.3: She wrote Homo Hierarchicus (1966).

x: Only 1 is correct: Irawati Karve is regarded as India's first woman sociologist. She divided India into four, not five, kinship zones; she wrote Kinship Organization in India (1953) - Homo Hierarchicus is Louis Dumont's; she held kinship to be the backbone of Indian social organisation.

st.3: In pre-independence Bihar the Kayasthas were a dominant caste along with the Bhumihars and Rajputs.

x: All three statements are correct: Srinivas developed the concept from Rampura, education and administrative jobs were later criteria, and the Bhumihars, Rajputs and Kayasthas (not Kurmis) dominated pre-independence Bihar.

st.2: In Thorner's scheme, Kisans own land and work it mainly with family labour.

x: All three statements are correct: Thorner classified agrarian classes by land rights and income, Kisans own land and use family labour (Maliks are the rent-living landlords), and Macaulay's Minute led to an English-educated middle class.

st.2: The sex ratio at birth fell from 917 to 904 (2021-23).
st.1: The sex ratio fell from 1020 in NFHS-4 to 991 in NFHS-5.

x: Only 4 is correct: women's LFPR was 37% in 2022-23. The sex ratio rose from 991 to 1020; the sex ratio at birth rose from 904 to 917; Haryana and Punjab, not Kerala and Tamil Nadu, are the most male-skewed.

st.2: The All-India Muslim League was founded at Dacca in 1906.

x: All three statements are correct: the Simla Deputation (October 1906) under the Aga Khan met Minto, the Muslim League was founded at Dacca in 1906, and Minto is called the Father of the Communal Electorate.

st.2: Religious fundamentalism cannot exist without inter-group conflict.

x: Only 3 is correct: fundamentalism is mainly doctrinal, communalism political. Group exclusiveness is a feature, not a cause, of fundamentalism; fundamentalism can exist without inter-group conflict.

st.2: Section 70 deals with intercourse by deceitful means such as a false promise of marriage or job.

x: Only 1 is correct: the BNS raised the gang-rape age from 16 to 18. Deceitful intercourse is Section 69 (Section 70 is gang rape); honour killing is prosecuted as murder under Section 103, not 101.

st.1: It was drafted by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
st.2: It came into force on 26 January 2013.

x: Only 4 is correct: the consent of a person below 18 is irrelevant under POCSO. It was drafted by the Ministry of Women and Child Development; it came into force on 14 November 2012; POCSO remains a separate law and was not merged into the BNS.

st.2: It added a new Section 14A on the rights of victims and witnesses.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The rights of victims and witnesses are in the new Chapter IVA, while Section 14A provides for appeals; trial in an Exclusive Special Court is to be completed within two months (60 days), not 90 days.

st.3: Census 2027 adds autism and dwarfism to its disability categories.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Movement disability, not seeing, was the largest category in 2011; Census 2027 adds acid attack, neurological and blood disorders but leaves out autism and dwarfism.

st.3: Under it Pakistan returned the Haji Pir Pass to India.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The ceasefire line became the Line of Control under the Simla Agreement (1972), not Tashkent; under Tashkent India returned the Haji Pir Pass to Pakistan.

st.3: India became a member of the FATF in 2010 but is not in the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. India, an FATF member since 2010, is also a member of the Asia/Pacific Group; its June 2024 mutual evaluation placed it under 'regular follow-up', not 'enhanced follow-up'.

st.3: The Rajiv Gandhi Action Plan for time-bound, universal disarmament was presented in 1988.

x: All three statements are correct: North Korea left the NPT in 2003, India calls the NPT 'nuclear apartheid', and the Rajiv Gandhi Action Plan was presented in 1988.

st.1: The 9th Indian Ocean Conference, organised by the India Foundation, was held in Mauritius.

x: All three statements are correct: the 9th Indian Ocean Conference of the India Foundation was held in Mauritius, IONS has 25 members and 9 observers, and its 9th Conclave of Chiefs was at Visakhapatnam in 2026.

st.1: It took charge on 24 August 1946.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Viceroy was ex-officio President and Nehru Vice-President of the Council. The Interim Government was announced on 24 August but took charge on 2 September 1946; the Muslim League joined in October 1946, not January 1947.

st.2: Janhit Abhiyan (2022) upheld the 103rd Amendment by a 3:2 majority.

x: All three statements are correct: Ashoka Kumar Thakur upheld the 93rd Amendment and OBC quota, Janhit Abhiyan upheld the EWS (103rd) Amendment 3:2, and Davinder Singh (6:1) allowed sub-classification of SCs and STs.

st.1: Article 14 is available only to citizens, not to foreigners.
st.2: Articles 15, 16, 19 and 21 are available only to citizens.

x: Only 3 is correct: Article 30 lets minorities establish educational institutions. Article 14 is available to all persons, foreigners included; the citizen-only rights are Articles 15, 16, 19, 29 and 30 - Article 21 covers all persons; Article 17 binds private persons too.

st.4: Dicey's first element means equality before the law, with all persons subject to the ordinary courts.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. India did not adopt Dicey's third principle, since rights here flow from the Constitution; Dicey's first element is the supremacy of regular law (no punishment except for a distinct breach of law) - equality before the law is his second.

st.3: The 44th Amendment's cut of the detention period without an Advisory Board report to two months has not been brought into force.

x: All three statements are correct: preventive detention is detention without trial on suspicion, it is meant for public order rather than routine law and order, and the 44th Amendment's two-month limit was never notified, so the three-month limit still applies.

st.1: Article 338B on the National Commission for Backward Classes was inserted by the 102nd Amendment.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 338B (NCBC) and Article 342A (SEBC lists) were both inserted by the 102nd Amendment (2018), and Article 16(4) was part of the original Constitution.

st.2: It is yet to be implemented in any State Legislative Assembly.

x: All three statements are correct: women's reservation under the 106th Amendment starts only after delimitation, it is yet to be implemented anywhere, and it received Presidential assent on 28 September 2023.

st.3: S.R. Bommai (1994) held that secularism is not part of the basic structure.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Kesavananda Bharati judges named secularism among the basic features. Secularism was a basic feature even before the 42nd Amendment added the word; S.R. Bommai reaffirmed it as part of the basic structure.

st.1: Its present strength of 543 is made up of 524 members from the States and 19 from the Union Territories.

x: All three statements are correct: the present 543 = 524 from the States + 19 from the UTs, the maximum under Article 81 is 550, and 552 (with two nominated Anglo-Indians) was the old maximum till 25 January 2020.

st.2: A member of the Panel presides when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent.

x: All three statements are correct: the Speaker nominates up to ten members to the Panel, a member presides when both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are absent (not when the Speaker's office is vacant), and failing them the House decides who presides.

st.3: The President decides the admissibility of questions, motions and resolutions in the Lok Sabha.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Speaker's Tenth Schedule decisions are subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan). The Leader of the Opposition needs one-tenth, not one-third, of the House; admissibility of questions and motions is decided by the Speaker, not the President.

st.2: Demands for grants are voted by both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council.
st.3: A Bill that originates in the Council and is rejected by the Assembly goes to a joint sitting of the two Houses.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Council can hold an Assembly Bill for three months on first passage and one month on second; demands for grants are voted only by the Assembly; a Council Bill rejected by the Assembly ends, as there is no joint sitting in a State Legislature.

st.2: A person may be a member of both Houses of a State Legislature at the same time.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Absence for 60 days without permission lets the House declare the seat vacant under Article 190(4) - it is not a disqualification under Article 191; no person can be a member of both Houses of a State Legislature at once.

st.3: Members of the Lok Sabha are elected directly, by the first-past-the-post system.

x: All three statements are correct: a CM who sits in the Council cannot vote, the 70th Amendment added the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies, and Lok Sabha members are elected directly by first-past-the-post (PR-STV is used for the President, not the Lok Sabha).

st.3: The 1984 Nadendla Bhaskara Rao episode was not a spell of President's Rule.

x: All three statements are correct: President's Rule was first imposed in Andhra State in 1954-55, Andhra Pradesh's first spell came in 1973 during Jai Andhra, and the 1984 Nadendla episode did not involve President's Rule.

st.2: In Sita Soren (2024) a seven-judge Bench held that legislators have no immunity for bribery connected with a speech or vote.

x: All three statements are correct: Raja Ram Pal upheld expulsion by the House, and a seven-judge Bench in Sita Soren denied immunity for bribery and overruled P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

st.4: Article 191 deals with the disqualifications for membership of Parliament.
st.2: A defection question under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the Election Commission.
st.1: A question of general (non-defection) disqualification of an MP is decided by the Speaker on the binding opinion of the Election Commission.

x: None of the statements is correct. General disqualification of an MP is decided by the President on the EC's binding opinion; defection is decided by the Speaker or Chairman as a tribunal; the Speaker need not consult the EC in defection cases; Article 191 covers State Legislatures (Article 102 covers Parliament).

st.2: Judicial review in India rests on 'procedure established by law', and in the USA on 'due process of law'.

x: All three statements are correct: residuary powers vest in the US States but in India's Union, Indian judicial review rests on 'procedure established by law' and American on 'due process', and the US 22nd Amendment (1951) limits presidential tenure.

st.1: Under Article 141, at least five judges must hear a case involving a substantial question of constitutional interpretation or a reference under Article 143.
st.4: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission.

x: Only 2 is correct: the curative petition was evolved in Rupa Ashok Hurra (2002). The five-judge rule is in Article 145(3), not Article 141; the Constitution does not define civil and criminal contempt - the 1971 Act does; the 1971 Act followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee, not the Sarkaria Commission.

st.4: Scandalising or lowering the authority of a court is civil contempt.
st.2: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 was the first law on contempt in India.

x: Only 3 is correct: wilful disobedience of a court's order is civil contempt. Contempt is defined in the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, not Article 129; the 1926 Act was the first major contempt law; scandalising a court is criminal, not civil, contempt.

st.1: The Indian Parliament is sovereign like the British Parliament, as its laws are not subject to judicial review.

x: Neither statement is correct. Parliament's laws are subject to judicial review, which limits its sovereignty; Parliament cannot amend the Constitution so as to destroy its basic structure.

st.1: The Lieutenant Governor may make regulations having the force of Acts of Parliament for the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.

x: Neither statement is correct. It is the President (Article 240), not the Lieutenant Governor, who makes such regulations; in Scheduled Areas it is the Governor who may bar or modify Acts of Parliament.

st.1: After 2019, the term of the NHRC Chairperson and members is 5 years or 70 years of age.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. After the 2019 amendment the NHRC term is 3 years (or 70 years of age), not 5; the NCM is a statutory body under the 1992 Act - Article 350-B is the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

st.2: In CPIL v Union of India (January 2026), Justice Nagarathna struck down Section 17A of the PC Act as violating Article 14, while Justice Viswanathan upheld it.

x: All three statements are correct: Subramanian Swamy (2014) struck down Section 6A, the CPIL ruling on Section 17A was a split verdict (Nagarathna striking it down, Viswanathan upholding it), and Vineet Narain struck down the Single Directive.

st.3: The Aspirational Districts Programme, launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in January 2018, covers 112 districts.
st.4: Alluri Sitharama Raju district ranked 1st in the Basic Infrastructure theme of the ADP (March 2026), while no Andhra Pradesh district remains in the programme.

x: Only 1 is correct: AP contributes about 70% of shrimp exports. The Water Plus cities were Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati, not Guntur; the ADP was launched by NITI Aayog; YSR Kadapa still remains in the programme.

st.2: AMRUT 2.0 (2021) is a scheme for Gram Panchayats under the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
st.1: The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program is a component of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen).
st.3: SVAMITVA uses drone maps to build an urban property-tax baseline for municipalities.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program is part of the revamped RGSA; AMRUT 2.0 is an urban scheme rewarding property-tax reform and municipal bonds; SVAMITVA builds a rural property-tax baseline; GVMC's ₹80 crore bonds were at 10%, not 8%.

st.3: Women MPs first crossed 10% of the House in the 15th Lok Sabha (2009).

x: All three statements are correct: the 17th Lok Sabha had 78 women (the highest), the 18th has 74, and women first crossed 10% in the 15th Lok Sabha (2009).

st.2: The Cantonments Act, 2006 replaced the Cantonments Act, 1956.
st.1: Cantonment Boards come under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

x: Only 4 is correct: MoHUA is the main ministry for urban local bodies. Cantonment Boards come under the Ministry of Defence; the 2006 Act replaced the Cantonments Act, 1924; Cantonment Boards are outside the three types of municipalities under Article 243Q.

st.3: The Cabinet Secretary acted as its Secretary.
st.1: It was set up on 6 August 1952 under an Act of Parliament.

x: None of the statements is correct. The NDC was set up on 6 August 1952 by an executive order (non-statutory); the Chief Justice of India was not a member; the Secretary of the Planning Commission, not the Cabinet Secretary, was its Secretary.

st.2: It targets green hydrogen production of 10 MMTA by 2030.
st.4: It has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and was approved by NITI Aayog in January 2023.

x: Only 1 is correct: MNRE is the nodal ministry. The target is 5 MMTA by 2030; the hubs are Kandla, Paradip and Tuticorin, not Haldia; the ₹19,744 crore mission was approved by the Union Cabinet, not NITI Aayog.

st.2: The Western DFC runs between Dadri and JNPT.

x: All three statements are correct: DFCs are freight-only lines built by DFCCIL, the Western DFC runs Dadri-JNPT and the Eastern DFC Ludhiana-Sonnagar/Dankuni.

st.2: It was notified on 14 October 2003 and became fully functional the same year.
st.1: It functions under the Ministry of Finance.

x: Only 3 is correct: the CCI has a Chairperson and 2 to 6 members. It functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs; though notified in October 2003, it became fully functional only in March 2009; the original 2002 Act allowed up to 10 members, not 6.

st.4: Max Weber classifies pressure groups as institutional, associational, non-associational and anomic.
st.1: A pressure group seeks to influence public policy mainly by contesting elections and seeking office.

x: Only 2 is correct: pressure groups are called the 'Anonymous Empire'. They influence policy without contesting elections; the Election Commission is a constitutional body, not a pressure group; the four-fold classification is Almond and Powell's, not Weber's.

st.4: In 1957 the UN Security Council took up India's resolution on peaceful co-existence.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Burma adopted Panchsheel in June 1954, not 1955; India's 1957 resolution on peaceful co-existence was taken up by the UN General Assembly, not the Security Council.

st.2: 96 works worth Rs 57,592.71 crore have been taken up, funded entirely by the Union Government.
st.1: India's first Justice City is planned in Visakhapatnam.
st.4: Amaravati Sangamam is coming up at Mangalagiri.

x: None of the statements is correct. The first Justice City is planned in Amaravati; the 96 works are funded also by World Bank-ADB (₹15,000 crore) and HUDCO (₹11,000 crore) loans; the World Bank and ADB give ₹15,000 crore, not ₹11,000 crore; Amaravati Sangamam is at Sakhamuru.

st.2: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission was launched in February 2015 at Kurubhat, Rajnandgaon (Chhattisgarh).

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. SPMRM was launched on 21 February 2016, not 2015; it aims at 300 Rurban clusters, not 500.

st.1: Madhya Pradesh has the highest share of underweight children.

x: All three statements are correct: Madhya Pradesh has the highest share of underweight children, Uttar Pradesh of stunted children (48.8%) and Bihar of wasted children (9.3%).
Match question, not a statement set: ICDS - 1975 (3), NIDDCP - 1992 (2), NP-NSPE (Mid-Day Meal) - 1995 (4), MAA - 2016 (1); the List-II years are left unchanged.

st.1: Net Domestic Product is GDP minus depreciation.

x: All three statements are correct: NDP = GDP minus depreciation, GNP = NNP plus depreciation, and 'NDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices minus depreciation' is wrong because net indirect taxes must also be removed.

st.3: It put public capital expenditure in FY26 at about 3.1% of GDP.

x: All three statements are correct: the Survey was prepared under CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran, projected FY27 growth at 6.8-7.2% (a 'year of adjustment'), and put FY26 public capex at about 3.1% of GDP.

st.1: In Gandhian thought, 'Ram Rajya' denotes an ideal, just society, not a Hindu state.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi's Ram Rajya means an ideal, just society rather than a Hindu state, Shriman Narayan Agarwal wrote the Gandhian Constitution for Free India, and the Janata strategy stressed agriculture and village industries.

st.3: The Nehru-Mahalanobis strategy created many jobs because it relied on capital-intensive industry.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Second Plan's planned outlay was Rs 4,800 crore and actual Rs 4,600 crore. The outlay was pruned because of rising prices and a foreign-exchange crisis, not falling inflation; capital-intensive industry created few jobs, not many.

st.2: It began a determined thrust towards export promotion of consumer goods industries.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Second Plan stressed industry and the public sector. It pushed import substitution of basic and capital goods, not export promotion of consumer goods; its targets were pruned because of a shortage, not a surplus, of foreign exchange.

st.1: A separate State Finance Commission is constituted for Municipalities.
st.2: The State Finance Commission constituted under Article 280 also reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y.

x: Neither statement is correct. There is no separate SFC for Municipalities - the SFC constituted under Article 243I for Panchayats also reviews municipal finances under Article 243Y; Article 280 is the Union Finance Commission.

st.2: From 1 October 2019 new floating-rate personal, retail and MSME loans had to be linked to the MCLR.
st.4: The draft Interest Rates on Loans and Advances Directions, 2026 were issued by SEBI.
st.1: The Janak Raj Internal Study Group (2017) on MCLR recommended continuing with internal benchmarks such as the MCLR.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Janak Raj group recommended an external benchmark; from 1 October 2019 such loans had to be linked to an external benchmark, not the MCLR; EBLR loans reprice faster, not slower; the 2026 draft Directions are the RBI's, not SEBI's.

st.1: NBFCs cannot borrow under the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility and raise short-term funds from banks and the money market.

x: All three statements are correct: NBFCs have no access to the LAF and raise short-term funds from banks and instruments such as commercial paper, they are companies registered under the Companies Act, and 100% automatic-route FDI is allowed except in Nidhi companies.

st.2: The idea was first mooted by the Narasimham Committee, whose report came in October 1969.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Nariman Committee proposed a Lead Bank for allotted districts. The RBI introduced the scheme in December 1969, not 1971; the idea came from the D.R. Gadgil Study Group (October 1969), not the Narasimham Committee.

st.1: It announced a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to review only the public sector banks.

x: Neither statement is correct. The High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat is to review the whole banking sector; the Budget announced the restructuring of PFC and REC, not NABARD and SIDBI.

st.3: In Budget 2026-27, corporation tax is the largest single source of every rupee received.

x: Only 1 is correct: recovery of loans and disinvestment are non-debt capital receipts. PSU dividends are non-tax revenue receipts, not capital receipts; the largest source in 2026-27 is borrowings and other liabilities (24 paise), followed by income tax (21) and corporation tax (18).

st.3: Borrowings and other liabilities, not income tax, are the largest single source of the Centre's receipts in the rupee.

x: All three statements are correct: direct taxes are about 6.9% and indirect about 4.3% of GDP, direct taxes are 61.2% of gross tax revenue, and borrowings (24 paise) rather than income tax (21 paise) are the largest receipt in the rupee.

st.2: Travel services are the largest part of India's services surplus.
st.3: India's services exports fell to about USD 341.06 billion in FY 2023-24.

x: Only 1 is correct: the FY25 services surplus of $188.8 billion financed about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit. Software, not travel, is the largest part of the surplus; services exports rose (by 4.85%) to USD 341.06 billion; remittances of $135.4 billion were about 3.5%, not 5.3%, of GDP.

st.3: Forests make up 18.28% of Andhra Pradesh's land-use classification.
st.1: India's net sown area was more than half of its geographical area in 2021-22.

x: Only 2 is correct: forest cover is 21.71% of India's area (ISFR 2021). Net sown area was about 42.8%, less than half; forests are 22.63% of AP's land-use classification (18.28% is its ISFR forest cover); AP's cropping intensity fell from 1.25 (2016-17) to 1.21 (2023-24).

st.1: The National Commission on Agriculture (1970) was chaired by C. Subramaniam and reported in 1976.

x: Only 3 is correct: BGREI under RKVY targets the eastern rice States. The NCA (1970) was chaired by N.R. Mirdha; the Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income was chaired by Ashok Dalwai, not M.S. Swaminathan.

st.3: Their share capital is held by the Centre, the sponsor bank and the State Government in the ratio 50:35:15.

x: All three statements are correct: five RRBs were set up on 2 October 1975, the first was Prathama Grameen Bank at Moradabad (Syndicate Bank), and share capital is held 50:35:15 by the Centre, sponsor bank and State.

st.1: Regional Rural Banks (1975) came after NABARD (1982).

x: Only 3 is correct: the Kisan Credit Card (1998) came after the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme. RRBs (1975) came before NABARD (1982); the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992-93) came after NABARD.

st.3: India's forex reserves touched a record USD 702.28 billion in November 2025.

x: All three statements are correct: post-1991 investment concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, many small units suffered from import competition, and reserves touched a record USD 702.28 billion in November 2025.

st.4: The target is USD 1 trillion of services exports within the USD 2 trillion export goal by 2047.
st.2: Services imports exceeded services exports of USD 387.5 billion in 2024-25.

x: Only 1 is correct: India is the 8th-largest services exporter. Services exports of USD 387.5 billion were far above imports (USD 198.7 billion), giving a surplus; software and business services are 77.8%, not 57.8%; the USD 1 trillion target is for 2030, not 2047.

st.4: The cropping intensity in 2023-24 was 1.25.
st.1: Agriculture and allied sectors make up about 60% of GVA (2025-26).
st.2: The State's geographical area is 126.97 lakh ha.

x: None of the statements is correct. Agriculture and allied are about 33% of GVA (60% is the population they support); the geographical area is 162.97 lakh ha; net sown area was 36.29% in 2024-25 (30.40% was the drought year 2023-24); cropping intensity in 2023-24 was 1.21 (1.25 was 2016-17).

st.2: 'Zero budget' means farmers receive no government support or subsidy.
st.4: ZBNF in Andhra Pradesh was renamed Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY).

x: Only 1 is correct: Subhash Palekar developed ZBNF in the mid-1990s. 'Zero budget' means no purchased inputs such as fertilisers and pesticides; AP launched ZBNF in 2016, not 2018; it was renamed APCNF - PKVY is a central scheme.

st.3: The AP Employment of Local Candidates in Industries/Factories Act, 2019 reserves 75% of jobs for locals.

x: All three statements are correct: IDP (4.0) adds an Escrow Guarantee, pavala vaddi leaves the unit paying 25 paise per Rs 100 per month, and the 2019 Act reserves 75% of jobs for locals.

st.1: It applied within the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation limits as well.
st.2: It provided for 30 skill development centres but no skill university.

x: Neither statement is correct. IDP 2020-23 did not apply within Vijayawada Municipal Corporation limits; it provided for 30 skill development centres and 2 skill universities.

st.2: It was first recognised under the SCRA in 1992.

x: Neither statement is correct. The BSE was set up in 1875 as the Native Share and Stock Brokers' Association (the NSE was set up in 1992 by financial institutions); it was the first exchange recognised under the SCRA, on 31 August 1957.

st.2: It began in 1988 as a statutory body.

x: Neither statement is correct. SEBI's parent law is the SEBI Act, 1992, not the SCRA, 1956; it began in 1988 as a non-statutory body and got statutory powers in 1992.

st.2: Its headquarters is in New Delhi.
st.1: On getting statutory powers in 1992 it took over from the Forward Markets Commission.

x: Only 4 is correct: Tuhin Kanta Pandey became Chairperson in March 2025. In 1992 SEBI took over from the Controller of Capital Issues (the FMC was merged into it only in 2015); its headquarters is in Mumbai; it functions under the Ministry of Finance, not Corporate Affairs.

st.2: The Prime Meridian passes through Mali.

x: All three statements are correct: the Arctic Circle (66½°N) crosses Norway, Sweden and Finland, the Prime Meridian passes through Mali (not Niger, which lies on the Tropic of Cancer), and Africa alone is crossed by the Equator and both Tropics.

st.1: The Standard Meridian of India is 82°30'E, so IST is 5 h 30 min behind GMT.

x: Neither statement is correct. At 82°30'E IST is 5 h 30 min ahead of GMT, not behind; the meridian passes through UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and AP, not West Bengal.

st.3: In Bowen's reaction series quartz crystallises first and olivine last.
st.2: Quartz is calcium carbonate and has a Mohs hardness of 7.

x: Only 4 is correct: on the Mohs scale topaz is 8 and talc 1. Feldspar makes up about half, not one-fourth, of the crust; quartz is silicon dioxide (calcite is calcium carbonate); in Bowen's series olivine crystallises first and quartz last.

st.4: Iron, at about 5%, is the most abundant metal.
st.3: Aluminium, at about 8.1%, is the second most abundant metal.

x: Only 1 is correct: oxygen (46.6%) is the most abundant element. Silicon (27.7%) is second but is not a metal; aluminium (8.1%) is the most abundant metal and iron (5%) the second.

st.1: Diego Garcia was with the Maldives until 1965, when it passed to the UK.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Diego Garcia was with Mauritius, not the Maldives, until 1965; Hong Kong was returned to China in 1997, not 1999.

st.4: The average annual rainfall of Andhra Pradesh is about 966 mm, higher than the national average.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The coast peaks in July while Rayalaseema peaks in October-November; AP's average of about 966 mm is below, not above, the national average.

st.1: About 90% of all atmospheric ozone lies in the troposphere.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Chapman cycle forms O3 from O2 split by UV. About 90% of ozone is in the stratosphere, not the troposphere; one Dobson Unit is 0.01 mm of pure ozone, not 1 mm.

st.3: Odisha lies on both the meridian and the Tropic of Cancer.
st.4: Chhattisgarh lies on the Tropic of Cancer but not on the meridian.
st.1: It is 82°30′ E, with Mirzapur in Madhya Pradesh as the reference place.

x: None of the statements is correct. Mirzapur is in Uttar Pradesh; the meridian does not pass through Telangana; Odisha lies on the meridian but not on the Tropic of Cancer; Chhattisgarh lies on both.

st.3: It placed Andhra Pradesh's coastline second, after Gujarat.
st.2: It counted 1,382 islands.

x: Only 1 is correct: the NHO and Survey of India carried it out. It counted 1,389 islands; AP's 1,053.07 km is third, after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; Srikakulam, not East Godavari, has AP's longest district coastline.

st.1: The Andhra Pradesh coast runs from Tada at Pulicat in the north to Ichchapuram (Srikakulam) in the south.
st.4: In the 2022 map, 9 districts touch the coast.

x: Only 2 is correct: Srikakulam has the longest district coastline. The coast runs from Ichchapuram in the north to Tada in the south; West Godavari, not Krishna, has the shortest (about 23 km); 12 districts touch the coast in the 2022 map.

st.2: As (monsoon with dry summer) is found along the Coromandel coast.

x: All three statements are correct: BShw covers NW Gujarat and parts of W Rajasthan and Punjab, As (dry summer) the Coromandel coast, and E/ET the high Himalaya; Cwg (dry winter) belongs to the Ganga plain.

st.1: The IMD functions under the Ministry of Science and Technology.
st.3: Mission Mausam was launched on 14 January 2025 to mark the IMD's centenary.
st.2: The National Monsoon Mission (2012) is implemented through ISRO and the IMD.

x: None of the statements is correct. The IMD is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences; the Monsoon Mission works through IITM Pune and the IMD, not ISRO; Mission Mausam (Rs 2,000 crore) marked the IMD's 150th year, not its centenary; the Bharat Forecast System works at 6 km, not 12 km.

st.3: The highest south-west monsoon rainfall falls in the north coastal districts.

x: All three statements are correct: the Sileru and Sabari valleys get 140-152 cm, the Hagari valley under 51 cm, and the highest south-west monsoon rain falls in north coastal AP (Rayalaseema gets the least).

st.1: The Brahmaputra is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because of its frequent floods.
st.2: Majuli in the Brahmaputra, in lower Assam, is the largest riverine island in the world.

x: Neither statement is correct. The Brahmaputra is the 'Sorrow of Assam' (the Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'); Majuli lies in upper, not lower, Assam.

st.1: The Kali (Kalinadi) of Karnataka is an east-flowing river that joins the Krishna.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Kabini flows east to the Kaveri. The Kali is west-flowing, rising near Diggi and entering the Arabian Sea at Karwar; the Tamraparni flows east into the Gulf of Mannar.

st.1: Amritdhara Falls is on the Hasdeo in Chhattisgarh.

x: All three statements are correct: Amritdhara Falls is on the Hasdeo in Chhattisgarh (not Jharkhand), Dasam Falls is on the Kanchi and Jonha Falls on the Rarhu in Jharkhand.

st.1: It drains into Pulicat Lake.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Tammileru has a dam on it. It drains into Kolleru Lake, not Pulicat; it runs between the Krishna and West Godavari (now NTR and Eluru) areas, not East Godavari.

st.1: The Machkund (upper Sileru) rises in the Madugula hills and joins the Indravati.
st.4: The Tunga and Bhadra rivers join to form the Vedavathi.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Gosthani rises in the Anantagiri hills and meets the sea near Bheemunipatnam. The Machkund joins the Sabari, not the Indravati; the Mahendratanaya rises in the Mahendragiri hills; the Vedavathi is formed by the Veda and Avathi (Tunga and Bhadra form the Tungabhadra).

st.2: It was approved in June 2021 with an outlay of ₹4,077 crore for 10 years.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The ₹4,077 crore outlay was for 5 years, not 10; the mission includes ocean energy and freshwater activities.

st.2: Haryana is the only tin-producing State, although Chhattisgarh has larger tin resources.
st.1: Hutti closed in 2001, and Kolar is now the main working gold mine.

x: Only 3 is correct: Odisha holds about 92-93% of nickel resources. Kolar closed in 2001 and Hutti is the main working mine; Chhattisgarh is the only tin producer though Haryana has larger resources; tungsten is mainly in Karnataka, not Kerala.

st.3: Nuclear plants in India run at a capacity factor of about 85-90%.

x: All three statements are correct: the PFBR at Kalpakkam went critical on 6 April 2026, the SHANTI Act 2025 repealed the 1962 Act and the CLNDA 2010, and nuclear plants run at about 85-90% (25-35% is wind).

st.4: The paper industry is labour-intensive, with low capital needs.
st.2: Recycled fibre makes up only about 7-10 per cent of the raw material of paper.
st.1: As per FAO, Brazil is now the top producer of wood pulp.

x: None of the statements is correct. The USA is the top pulp producer (Brazil is the top exporter); recycled fibre is about 71-75% of paper's raw material; India's per capita paper use is far below 57 kg (around 15 kg); the paper industry is capital-intensive.

st.4: Andhra Pradesh is the largest exporting State as per the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26.
st.2: Under ODOP, Narsapur crochet laces represent West Godavari and Budithi brass represents Vizianagaram.

x: Only 1 is correct: Anantapur has the most Udyam MSMEs. Budithi brass represents Srikakulam; the CII Partnership Summit 2025 was at Visakhapatnam, not Amaravati; AP is the 6th, not the largest, exporting State.

st.1: It is being developed by the Adani Group under PPP-DBFOT.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The developer is GMR, not Adani; APADCL is 100% State-owned, not 49%.

st.1: The Kharagpur-Visakhapatnam-Amaravati expressway has been completed.
st.2: The completed 125-km Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla PPP road links NH-44 and NH-16.

x: Only 3 is correct: NH works of over Rs 1.40 lakh crore are targeted by 2029. Only a DPR has been ordered for the Kharagpur-Visakhapatnam-Amaravati expressway; the Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla road links NH-65 and NH-16; the 2017 Hyperloop MoU was with Hyperloop Transportation Technologies, not Virgin Hyperloop One.

st.1: In 1951, India's literacy rate was 18.33%, with female literacy at about 8.9%.

x: All three statements are correct: 1951 literacy was 18.33% (male 27.2%, female about 8.9%), growth in 1891-1921 was about 0.19% a year, and life expectancy around 1951 was about 32 years.

st.2: Its medium-term objective is to bring TFR to 2.1 by 2010.

x: All three statements are correct: NPP 2000's immediate objective is the unmet need for contraception and health infrastructure, the medium-term objective TFR 2.1 by 2010, and the long-term objective a stable population by 2045.

st.2: The all-time low was recorded in 1991.

x: All three statements are correct: the sex ratio fell in most Censuses from 1901 to 1991, hit its all-time low (927) in 1991, and has risen since.

st.2: Registered workers get a 12-digit Universal Account Number.

x: All three statements are correct: e-Shram was launched on 26 August 2021, gives a 12-digit UAN, and had about 31.89 crore workers by 18 August 2026.

st.2: With about 1,053 km, it has the third longest coastline among Indian States.

x: All three statements are correct: about 70.5% of AP lived in rural areas in 2011, its 1,053 km coast is third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (2023-24 remeasurement), and it is now the 7th largest State by area.

st.2: Goudu, Nayak and Valmiki are STs throughout the State.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Goudu, Nayak and Valmiki are STs only in the Agency tracts; the February 2024 amendment added Porja sub-groups (Bonda Porja, Khond Porja, Parangiperja), not Koya and Gond sub-groups.

st.1: Nagaland (51.5%) is the north-eastern exception to the region's low urbanisation.

x: Only 3 is correct: Srikakulam was AP's least urbanised district (16.16%). The north-eastern exception is Mizoram, not Nagaland; Visakhapatnam (47.45%) was the most urbanised district, with Krishna second.

st.4: The revised IIP (June 2026) was released by the Reserve Bank of India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The new series lowered GDP levels by 3-4%, not raised them; the IIP is compiled and released by the NSO (MoSPI), not the RBI.

st.2: Silent Valley National Park lies in the Nilgiri hills of Kerala and is drained by the Kunthipuzha.

x: All three statements are correct: the Ramganga, Sonanadi and Kosi flow through Corbett, Silent Valley lies in the Nilgiris (Palakkad, Kerala) drained by the Kunthipuzha, and Indravati National Park is noted for the wild buffalo.

st.3: The glaciation of peninsular India, recorded in the Talchir tillite, took place in the Permo-Carboniferous (Gondwana) ice age.

x: All three statements are correct: the Little Ice Age is placed at about 1550-1850, 950-1250 AD was the Medieval Warm Period, and the Talchir tillite records the Permo-Carboniferous glaciation (Pleistocene glaciers reached only the Himalaya).

st.3: Nigeria has the world's highest TFR, about 6.6.
st.1: The replacement-level total fertility rate (TFR) is 2.1, while the world average is now below it.
st.2: Japan recorded the world's lowest TFR, 0.72, in 2023.

x: None of the statements is correct. The world average TFR (2.2) is still above the replacement level of 2.1; the lowest TFR (0.72, 2023) was South Korea's; the highest (about 6.6) is Niger's, not Nigeria's; Monaco has the oldest, not the youngest, median age.

st.1: India is about the 6th largest producer and 2nd largest consumer of natural rubber; Karnataka gives 70-75%.
st.3: AP ranks first in India in oil palm, papaya, cocoa and arecanut.

x: Only 2 is correct: Karnataka produces about 71% of India's coffee and AP is 4th. Kerala, not Karnataka, gives 70-75% of natural rubber; AP leads in oil palm, papaya, cocoa and chillies, but not arecanut (Karnataka leads); Assam, not AP, is the largest tea producer.

st.3: Its regional headquarters for Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka is at Hyderabad.

x: Only 2 is correct: the NDRF Academy is at Nagpur. The NDRF was raised in 2006 with 8 battalions (12 came by 2017); its regional headquarters for AP, Telangana and Karnataka is at Vijayawada, not Hyderabad.

st.3: Cyber attacks and space weather are classed as emerging hazards.

x: All three statements are correct: industrial, chemical and nuclear disasters are man-made, floods worsened by deforestation are socio-natural, and cyber attacks and space weather are emerging hazards (not meteorological).

st.4: Individual Indian patentees together have filed more patents than CSIR.
st.1: The Intellectual Property Appellate Board, set up on 15 September 2003, still hears patent appeals.

x: Only 3 is correct: SIPP 2016 gives start-ups free IP filing facilitation. The IPAB (2003) was abolished in 2021; patent appeals now go to the High Courts, not the Supreme Court; CSIR has filed more patents than all individual Indian patentees together.

st.1: It is run jointly by DRDO and ISRO since 2015.
st.4: It planned 10 systems.

x: Only 3 is correct: NSM machines form the National Supercomputing Grid over the NKN. The NSM is run by DST and MeitY; it is implemented by C-DAC Pune and IISc Bengaluru, not IIT Bombay; it planned 40 systems.

st.2: The retail pilot (e₹-R) began on 1 December 2022 in a closed user group in Mumbai, New Delhi, Bengaluru and Bhubaneswar.

x: All three statements are correct: the wholesale pilot began on 1 November 2022 for G-sec settlement, the retail pilot on 1 December 2022 in Mumbai, New Delhi, Bengaluru and Bhubaneswar (not Hyderabad), and the RBI's CBDC concept note came in October 2022.

st.1: The POEM platform built on the PSLV's fourth stage was conceived and realised by VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram.

x: All three statements are correct: POEM, on the spent PS4 stage, is VSSC's work (not URSC's), Agnikul Cosmos is a Chennai start-up incubated at IIT Madras, and Bellatrix's green propulsion flew on POEM-3 under DRDO's TDF.

st.1: The Open-RAN 5G partnership in India is between Vodafone Idea and Tata.

x: Only 3 is correct: C-DOT was set up in 1984. The Open-RAN 5G partnership is between Airtel and Tata; the TTDF gets 5%, not 10%, of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections.

st.2: GSAT-7R (CMS-03), launched on LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025, serves the Indian Navy.

x: All three statements are correct: GSAT-7 (Rukmini) was launched by Ariane-5 in 2013, GSAT-7R (CMS-03) serves the Navy, replacing GSAT-7 (GSAT-7A serves the Air Force), and it is the heaviest Indian communication satellite.

st.3: GSAT-1, the first payload of the GSLV (2001), was a student satellite.
st.1: WESAT, the first satellite fully built by women students, was made by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Bengaluru.

x: None of the statements is correct. The LBS Institute of Technology for Women is in Thiruvananthapuram; WESAT measures solar UV, not groundwater recharge; GSAT-1 was a full-scale ISRO communication satellite, not a student satellite.

st.1: The APXS found the lunar soil rich in iron and magnesium and poor in aluminium.

x: All three statements are correct: the APXS found the soil rich in iron and magnesium (poor in aluminium), the LRA is a passive NASA instrument, and the LIBS confirmed sulphur in situ.

st.1: iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) was launched by the Prime Minister in April 2018 at Aero India, Bengaluru.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. iDEX was launched by the PM in April 2018 at DefExpo near Chennai, not Aero India; the DIO was set up by HAL and BEL, not DRDO.

st.2: In AP's service-delivery chain, MeeSeva came before e-Pragati.

x: All three statements are correct: e-Seva (2001) set up India's first integrated citizen service centres, MeeSeva (2011) came before e-Pragati, and RTGS includes the Data Lake, Data Lens and a Command & Control Centre.

st.1: Echo chambers and filter bubbles weaken fake news by exposing users to diverse views.
st.2: Deepfakes are a form of malinformation, being genuine content shared to cause harm.

x: None of the statements is correct. Echo chambers and filter bubbles strengthen fake news; deepfakes are AI-made fake audio or video, not genuine content; false content spread without intent to deceive is misinformation - malinformation is genuine information shared to harm.

st.1: APSWAN links the Secretariat with district headquarters but not with mandal headquarters; it became operational in November 2010.
st.2: APSWAN was replaced by AP FiberNet on 1 May 2021.

x: Only 3 is correct: APSCAN is the Velagapudi Secretariat campus network (2016). APSWAN links the Secretariat with district and mandal headquarters; on 1 May 2021 it was upgraded to the software-defined APSDWAN; the State Data Centre is at Mangalagiri (Pi Data Centers), not Visakhapatnam.

st.2: India, Russia and China are signatories to it.

x: Neither statement is correct. The Budapest Convention was adopted under the Council of Europe, not the UN; India, Russia and China have not signed it.

st.1: The Cyber Commandos programme under CERT-In was launched in 2024.

x: Only 2 is correct: banks may refund frauds below Rs 50,000 without a court order. The Cyber Commandos programme (2024) is under I4C, not CERT-In; frozen funds are to be released within 90 days, not 180.

st.1: The draft Rules were released by the Ministry of Law and Justice on 3 January 2025.
st.4: The Consent Manager provisions applied at once from November 2025.

x: Only 2 is correct: the final DPDP Rules were notified on 14 November 2025. The draft (3 January 2025) came from MeitY, not the Law Ministry; full compliance is due by May 2027, not May 2026; the Consent Manager provisions apply from November 2026.

st.1: The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 was issued by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The draft policy was issued by the Ministry of Power, not MNRE; it targets 100 GW, not 50 GW, of pumped storage by 2047.

st.4: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 as a regulator that fixes electricity tariffs.
st.2: The Act made generation a licensed activity and kept the SEBs as integrated utilities.
st.1: The Electricity Act, 2003 was notified on 10 June 2003 by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Electricity Act (10 June 2003) is a Ministry of Power law; it delicensed generation, unbundled the SEBs and allowed open access; APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998; APTEL (2004) is an appellate tribunal, not a tariff regulator.

st.2: Nuclear power is non-fossil but is not classified as renewable.

x: All three statements are correct: MNRE has counted large hydro as renewable since 2019, nuclear power is non-fossil but not renewable, and nuclear and geothermal energy are not derived from the Sun.

st.2: BS-III norms were first applied nationwide on 1 April 2005.

x: Only 1 is correct: BS-II was first applied in Delhi from 1 April 2000. BS-III came on 1 April 2005 only in the NCR and 10 other cities (nationwide in 2010); BS-IV came in 2010 in 13 cities, not 23.

st.3: IEC Class III turbines are designed for high-wind sites.

x: Only 2 is correct: the Betz limit is 16/27 (about 59.3%). Wind power varies with the cube, not the square, of wind speed; Class III turbines are for low-wind sites (Class I for high-wind).

st.3: The phosphorus cycle is a gaseous cycle whose main reservoir is the atmosphere.

x: Only 1 is correct: the nitrogen cycle is gaseous and the sulphur cycle sedimentary. The main reservoir of sedimentary cycles is the Earth's crust, not ocean water; the phosphorus cycle is sedimentary, with no atmospheric phase and phosphate rock as its reservoir.

st.1: It was drawn up by Rodgers and Panwar of the Botanical Survey of India in 1988.
st.2: India includes two biogeographic realms – the Palearctic and the Afrotropical.

x: Only 3 is correct: India's zones fall into 5 biomes. Rodgers and Panwar were of the Wildlife Institute of India; the two realms are the Palearctic and the Indo-Malayan; India has 10 biogeographic zones (25 is the number of provinces).

st.2: A warming Arctic is becoming harder for alien plants to colonise.
st.1: Warming helps corals recover from bleaching and slows ocean acidification.

x: Neither statement is correct. Warming causes coral bleaching and goes with ocean acidification; a warming Arctic is opening up to alien plants.

st.3: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ Project in Mizoram is India's first community REDD+ project, Plan Vivo certified.

x: Only 1 is correct: it gives the full meaning of REDD+. UN-REDD (2008) is run by UNDP, FAO and UNEP, not the World Bank; the Khasi Hills project is in Meghalaya, not Mizoram.

st.1: Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal GBF seeks to conserve 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030.

x: Only 3 is correct: the HAC is co-chaired by Costa Rica, France and the UK, and India joined in 2021. Target 2 is restoring 30% of degraded ecosystems - conserving 30% of land and oceans is Target 3; 30x30 is a biodiversity, not a renewable-energy, target.

st.1: The yellowing and loss of lustre of the Taj marble, called 'marble cancer', is linked to carbon monoxide, notably from the Mathura refinery.
st.2: The Taj Trapezium Zone, covering about 10,400 sq km, includes Sanchi.

x: None of the statements is correct. Marble cancer is caused by sulphur dioxide, not carbon monoxide; the 10,400 sq km Taj Trapezium Zone covers Agra and Fatehpur Sikri, not Sanchi; the coal and coke ban came in M.C. Mehta (1996), not 2006.

st.2: Stratospheric ozone shields the Earth from infrared radiation.

x: Only 1 is correct: ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant. Stratospheric ozone shields the Earth from UV, not infrared, radiation; ground-level ozone is formed photochemically, not emitted directly by vehicles.

st.1: The Yamuna Action Plan is a bilateral project of India with Japan.

x: All three statements are correct: the Yamuna Action Plan (1993) is an India-Japan project, it aimed at sewage and industrial pollution in the Delhi stretch, and the NRCP (1995) extended the GAP to rivers beyond the Ganga basin.

st.2: India must freeze HFC consumption in 2024.
st.4: China is in the same group (Group 2) as India.

x: Only 1 is correct: India's baseline is 2024-26. India freezes in 2028 (2024 is Group 1's freeze); its 85% cut is due by 2047, not 2045; China is in Group 1, while Pakistan is with India in Group 2.

st.3: Benefit sharing under the PPV&FR Act is through the National Gene Fund.

x: All three statements are correct: T-GURT seed stays fertile with a chemically switched trait, the PPV&FR Act bars registration of GURT varieties, and benefit sharing is through the National Gene Fund.

st.2: Its target is 1,500 drones.
st.4: Central assistance is 50% of the drone cost, up to Rs 8 lakh.
st.1: It provides drones to individual women farmers rather than to self-help groups.

x: None of the statements is correct. Namo Drone Didi gives drones to women self-help groups; its target is 15,000 drones; its outlay is Rs 1,261 crore, not Rs 2,817 crore; central assistance is 80% of the cost, up to Rs 8 lakh.

st.2: Global sea level rose by about 20 cm during 1901-2018, and the rate of rise has since halved.
st.1: Its principal cause is the melting of floating icebergs and sea ice.

x: Only 3 is correct: inhabited Kiribati and Tuvalu are at risk. The principal causes are thermal expansion and melting glaciers and ice sheets - floating ice adds little; the rate of rise has doubled (to about 4.5 mm a year), not halved; the IPCC projects about 0.43-0.84 m by 2100, not one metre by 2070.

st.2: Nitrogen trifluoride (NF3) was added only for the second commitment period.

x: All three statements are correct: the first period called for about 5% below 1990, NF3 was added only for the second period (the original six gases did not include it), and the Doha Amendment set 18% below 1990 for 2013-2020.

st.1: It was announced by the Prime Minister at COP27, Sharm el-Sheikh.
st.2: It includes 250 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030.
st.4: It includes meeting 60% of energy requirements from renewables by 2030.

x: None of the statements is correct. Panchamrit was announced at COP26, Glasgow (1 November 2021); it includes 500 GW of non-fossil capacity, a cut of 1 billion tonnes in projected emissions by 2030 (not 2047) and 50% of energy needs from renewables by 2030.

st.3: The World Conservation Strategy of 1980 was launched by IUCN with UNEP and WWF.

x: All three statements are correct: Silent Spring (1962) set off the modern environmental movement, The Limits to Growth (1972) was prepared for the Club of Rome by an MIT team, and the 1980 World Conservation Strategy came from IUCN with UNEP and WWF.

st.1: The Forest Principles adopted at Rio are a non-binding statement on forests.

x: All three statements are correct: the Forest Principles are non-binding, the Rio Declaration set out 27 principles, and the CBD (with the UNFCCC) was opened for signature at Rio.

st.2: Bti is a fungal bio-larvicide.
st.1: Gambusia affinis (mosquito fish) controls mosquitoes by eating the adult insects.

x: Only 4 is correct: Verily's 'Debug' released Wolbachia-carrying male Culex quinquefasciatus. Gambusia eats mosquito larvae, not adults; Bti is a bacterial, not fungal, larvicide; Wolbachia is naturally absent in Aedes aegypti and Anopheles.

st.2: India's under-five mortality has fallen by about 78% since 1990.

x: All three statements are correct: India's MMR has fallen about 86% and under-five mortality about 78% since 1990, and the probability of dying from an NCD rose in 2001-2019 for women over 40 and men over 55.

st.3: Insecticide-treated bed nets and indoor residual spraying are among the main malaria-control tools of the NVBDCP.

x: All three statements are correct: the Maldives was SEAR's first malaria-free country, Sri Lanka was certified in 2016, and LLINs and indoor residual spraying (not antibiotic prophylaxis) are NVBDCP tools.

st.1: India's national target for TB elimination is 2025.

x: All three statements are correct: India's national TB-elimination target is 2025 (the SDG target is 2030), Ni-kshay is the Central TB Division's patient management system, and Ni-kshay Mitras adopt patients under the PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan.

st.1: Mission Indradhanush (December 2014) aims at 90% full immunisation.

x: All three statements are correct: Mission Indradhanush targets 90% full immunisation, eVIN (MoHFW with UNDP) digitises vaccine stocks and monitors the cold chain, and U-WIN is a digital registry of routine immunisation.

st.4: A hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle emits carbon dioxide along with water.
st.3: C-V2X vehicle communication is based on Wi-Fi.

x: Only 1 is correct: NavIC is India's own satellite navigation system. DSRC is Wi-Fi based, while C-V2X uses 4G/5G cellular networks; a hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle emits only water.

st.1: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's internet connections rose from 25.15 crore (2004) to 96.96 crore (2014).
st.2: BharatNet fibre already reaches every village in India.
st.3: CM Chandrababu Naidu and Mukesh Ambani discussed an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.

x: None of the statements is correct. Internet connections rose from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 96.96 crore in 2024; BharatNet reaches 2.18 lakh gram panchayats, not every village; the undersea cable talks were with Sunil Mittal; BhashaNet promotes .Bharat in Devanagari, not Telugu.

st.3: A modem is a Physical-layer device.

x: All three statements are correct: the OSI model has seven layers with Application at the top, Session lies just below Presentation, and a modem works at the Physical layer.

st.3: In the address mark.sttol@ITdesk.info, the domain name is mark.sttol.

x: Only 1 is correct: SMTP sends mail, POP3 and IMAP receive it. BCC hides recipients' addresses from one another; in mark.sttol@ITdesk.info the domain is ITdesk.info (mark.sttol is the user name).

st.4: Its logo showed a peacock with a "Namaste" motif.
st.1: It was held at Jio World Centre, Mumbai, on 12–13 September 2026.
st.3: India handed over the BRICS chair to Russia for 2027.

x: None of the statements is correct. The summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; it was India's fourth, not fifth, Chairship; the chair passed to China for 2027; the logo showed a lotus, not a peacock.

st.1: The IFC, not the AIIB, is one of the five arms of the World Bank Group.

x: All three statements are correct: the five World Bank Group arms are IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID (the AIIB is not one), MC14 was held at Yaoundé in March 2026, and 66 members decided to implement the e-commerce agreement.

st.1: The UAE left OPEC but stayed in OPEC+ from 1 May 2026.
st.3: OPEC+ (12 OPEC + 10 non-OPEC countries) accounts for about 29% of global crude.

x: Only 2 is correct: the UAE had been in OPEC since 1967. It left both OPEC and OPEC+ from 1 May 2026; OPEC+ accounts for about 59% of global crude; OPEC (1960) is headquartered at Vienna, not Riyadh.

st.2: Under Article 8 of the Rome Statute, ecocide is already listed as a separate core crime.
st.4: Chile and Vietnam are the only countries with ecocide laws.

x: Only 1 is correct: Arthur W. Galston coined the term in 1970. Ecocide is not yet a separate Rome Statute crime - Article 8 treats environmental damage as a war crime only if intentional, widespread, long-term and severe; India has no ecocide law; Russia, Ukraine, France and Belgium also have such laws.

st.3: The initial offshore-wind zones are Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

x: All three statements are correct: the Social Security Agreement covers postings of up to 36 months, the Offshore Wind Taskforce was launched at the 4th Energy Dialogue, and the initial zones are Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (not Andhra Pradesh).

st.2: ECOSOC has 54 members, but the High-level Political Forum on the SDGs is run by UNEP.
st.4: India chairs the Colombo Process for 2024–26, for the third time.

x: Only 1 is correct: the UN Human Rights Council was set up in 2006. ECOSOC, not UNEP, runs the HLPF; the Colombo Process secretariat is hosted by IOM, not UNHCR; India chairs the process for the first time.

st.1: India and the GCC signed the Terms of Reference to restart FTA talks at New Delhi in February 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: the India-GCC FTA Terms of Reference were signed in New Delhi in February 2026, the GCC (1981) is headquartered at Riyadh, and AYUSH got annexures in the Oman and New Zealand agreements.

st.1: It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 20 May 2025.

x: Neither statement is correct. The Pandemic Agreement was adopted by the World Health Assembly, not the UN General Assembly; it opens for signature only after its pathogen access and benefit-sharing (PABS) annex is adopted.

st.2: India has ratified all five treaties.

x: Neither statement is correct. India has signed but not ratified the 1979 Moon Agreement, so it has signed all five treaties but ratified only four.

st.1: The UPU, set up in 1865, is the oldest UN agency.

x: Only 3 is correct: ICAO was created by the Chicago Convention and has a 36-member Council. The oldest UN agency is the ITU (1865), not the UPU (1874); UNESCO's Executive Board has 58 members, not 36.

st.2: The 8th India–Japan Defence Policy Dialogue was held in Tokyo in July 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: Rajnath Singh and Shinjiro Koizumi concluded a maritime security arrangement in August 2026, the 8th Defence Policy Dialogue was held in Tokyo in July 2026, and Startup India began on 16 January 2016 with DPIIT as nodal body.

st.2: The US did not impose CAATSA sanctions on India over its 2018 S-400 deal with Russia.
