x: All three statements are correct: CAATSA (2017) targets Russia, Iran and North Korea, the US did not sanction India over the S-400 deal, and secondary sanctions target third countries.

st.3: Under the UK Tobacco and Vapes Bill, persons born after 1 January 2000 can never legally buy tobacco.

x: Only 1 is correct: Canada was the first non-European country at an EPC summit. The EPC (2022) is not an EU institution - it includes the UK, Türkiye and Norway; the Tobacco and Vapes Bill covers persons born after 1 January 2009, not 2000.

st.3: The INSTC linked to it runs to Russia, Central Asia and Europe, not to Southeast Asia.

x: All three statements are correct: Chabahar lies on the Gulf of Oman outside the Persian Gulf, it is Iran's only oceanic port, and the 7,200-km INSTC links India, Iran, Russia, Central Asia and Europe.

st.3: NATO's 'Arctic Sentry' is not a military operation and has no permanently stationed troops.

x: All three statements are correct: the Weimar Triangle (1991) has no formal structure, the EU's first Legal Gateway office outside its members is in New Delhi, and Arctic Sentry is a security effort without permanent troops.

st.3: UNCLOS Article 123 provides for cooperation in semi-enclosed seas like the Palk Bay.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1974 treaty placed Katchatheevu under Sri Lanka, Sri Lanka banned bottom trawling in 2017, and UNCLOS Article 123 (not 121, which covers islands) deals with semi-enclosed seas.

st.2: The India Semiconductor Mission was set up in 2021 under MeitY.

x: All three statements are correct: ISM 1.0 had approved 4 units by 2024, the ISM was set up in 2021 under MeitY (not Commerce), and Semicon 2.0 was notified on 31 August 2026.

st.3: It includes all engine systems, the thrust chamber included.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The test ran 35 seconds in all but only 5 seconds at full rated level; the PHTA includes all engine systems except the thrust chamber.

st.3: IIT Bombay's low-cost device works because viscous blood spreads shorter when smeared.

x: All three statements are correct: the severity score came from CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad, the elimination mission was launched on 1 July 2023 with a 2047 goal, and IIT Bombay's device uses the fact that viscous blood spreads shorter.

st.2: HSL was established in 1941 and functions under the Ministry of Defence.

x: All three statements are correct: INS Surya was launched at HSL on 6 October 2026, HSL (1941) is under the Ministry of Defence (not Ports and Shipping), and it is building five Fleet Support Ships of about 43,500 tonnes.

st.1: The 'Greater Than Us' campaign aims to raise USD 100 million by March 2029.

x: Neither statement is correct. The 'Greater Than Us' campaign aims to raise USD 1 billion, not USD 100 million, by March 2029; IIT Kanpur (1959) was set up with the help of nine US universities (KIAP), not UK universities.

st.2: Armenia was the first foreign user of the Akash system.

x: All three statements are correct: the Akash (BDL and BEL) has gone to Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, Armenia was its first foreign user (the Philippines was BrahMos's first buyer), and BrahMos Aerospace is a 1998 DRDO-NPO Mashinostroyenia JV.

st.2: The 500 MWe sodium-cooled reactor was built by BHAVINI.

x: All three statements are correct: the PFBR's criticality on 6 April 2026 took India into Stage II, the 500 MWe sodium-cooled reactor was built by BHAVINI (not NPCIL), and criticality (k = 1) goes back to Leo Szilard (1933).

st.2: The USA and China have laws making technology giants pay news publishers.

x: Only 1 is correct: DPIIT formed a committee on copyright and AI. It is Australia and Canada, not the USA and China, that have laws making tech giants pay news publishers; fair use permits limited use without permission and without payment.

st.2: The Bharat 6G Alliance signed MoUs with NASSCOM and NASA.
st.1: India's 6G vision targets peak speeds of about 10-20 Gbps using terahertz frequencies.

x: Only 3 is correct: India joined Denmark, Sweden, South Korea and China as makers of their own 4G stack. The 6G vision targets about 1 Tbps (10-20 Gbps is 5G); the Bharat 6G Alliance's MoUs were with NASSCOM and the European Space Agency, not NASA; the 4G Saturation Mission is funded by Digital Bharat Nidhi, not PM-WANI.

st.2: It is implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

x: All three statements are correct: the RBM scheme is extended to 2030-31 with ₹2,183 crore, it is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti (not MoEFCC), and India has about 4% of world freshwater for about 17% of its population.

st.2: Tree-rich areas such as Delhi Ridge are 1–3°C cooler.

x: All three statements are correct: UHI intensity in Indian cities is 2-10°C, tree-rich areas such as Delhi Ridge are 1-3°C cooler (6-8°C is the extra heat of surface hotspots), and SDG 11 and SDG 15 are Sustainable Cities and Life on Land.

st.1: 111 sitting legislators in 17 States/UTs, all of them MLAs, changed parties.
st.2: West Bengal recorded the highest number of such legislators, and Telangana was 3rd.

x: None of the statements is correct. The 111 included 26 Lok Sabha MPs and 7 Rajya Sabha MPs besides 78 MLAs; Nagaland (32) was highest, with West Bengal (20) second and Telangana (9) third; the Tenth Schedule came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

st.2: Globally, coal stayed ahead of renewables in electricity generation.
st.1: India's GHG emissions rose about 7.6% in 2025, in step with its economic growth.

x: Neither statement is correct. India's emissions fell 0.2% in 2025 despite about 7.6% growth; globally renewables (33.5%) overtook coal (33.2%) in electricity generation.

st.1: There are eight nuclear-armed states.

x: Only 2 is correct: SIPRI, in Stockholm, was set up in 1966. There are nine nuclear-armed states, not eight; India's about 190 warheads were about 20 more, not fewer, than Pakistan's.

st.1: Only 8 of 28 States exceeded the 3% of GSDP fiscal deficit limit.
st.4: In 14 States the fiscal deficit fell by 25% or more over 2023–24.

x: Only 3 is correct: Meghalaya had the highest fiscal deficit (8.69%). 18 of 28 States exceeded the 3% limit; revenue-surplus States fell from 16 to 13; in 14 States the deficit rose, not fell, by 25% or more.

st.2: The support ratio (working-age adults per elderly person) rose from 5.2 in 2001 to 8.4 in 2026.
st.1: By 2050 about 1 in 5 Indians will be aged 60+, and about 70% of the elderly will live in urban areas.

x: None of the statements is correct. About 70% of the elderly will live in rural, not urban, areas; the support ratio fell from 8.4 (2001) to 5.2 (2026); the 2007 Act is administered by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not Health.

st.1: The report is brought out by the Centre for Science and Environment, founded by Anil Agarwal.

x: All three statements are correct: the report is by CSE, founded by Anil Agarwal (not Sunita Narain), India had extreme weather on 99% of days in 2025, and Madhya Pradesh had the highest forest diversion (about 22%).

st.3: Andhra Pradesh's urban TFR was higher than its rural TFR.
st.1: India's Infant Mortality Rate was 30.

x: None of the statements is correct. India's IMR in SRS 2024 was 24 (30 was 2019); AP's IMR (18) was higher than Telangana's (17); AP's urban TFR (1.3) was lower than its rural TFR (1.5).

st.4: It was praised for fully capturing regional and subject diversity.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Tamil Nadu, not Karnataka, had the most top-100 institutions; NIRF 2025 was criticised for neglecting regional and subject diversity.

st.2: BibloRed of Colombia won a Confucius Prize for Escuelas LEO in Bogotá.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. BibloRed won a King Sejong Prize, not a Confucius Prize; Hat Yai won a Confucius Prize, not a King Sejong Prize, for 'Language for Life'.

st.1: They were for films certified by the CBFC in 2025; the ceremony was on 19 March 2026 (Sankranti).

x: Only 2 is correct: Best Film went to 'Raju Weds Rambhai'. The 19 March 2026 ceremony was on Ugadi, not Sankranti; Best Actress went to Rashmika, not Sai Pallavi.

st.3: The first recipient of the Lata Deenanath Mangeshkar Award (2022) was Narendra Modi.

x: All three statements are correct: Jayanthi Kumaresh gets the Sangeetha Kalanidhi 2026, the Music Academy dates from 18 August 1928, and the first Lata Deenanath Mangeshkar Award (2022) went to Narendra Modi.

st.2: The Best Actor (Critics) award went to Teja Sajja.

x: All three statements are correct: Allu Arjun and Sukumar won Best Actor and Best Director for Pushpa 2, Teja Sajja (Hanu-Man) won Best Actor (Critics), and the awards were held in Kochi.

st.1: Boyi Bhimanna won in 1975 for Gabbilam.

x: Only 3 is correct: Madhurantakam Narendra won in 2022 for Manodharmaparagam. Boyi Bhimanna won in 1975 for Gudisale Kalipotunnayi; Gabbilam is Gurram Jashuva's work, and he did not win the award for it.

st.2: There is no limit on the number of living Fellows.
st.4: Pasumarthi Rattaiah Sarma (Kuchipudi, Andhra Pradesh) received the Akademi Puraskar, not the Akademi Ratna, in August 2026.
st.1: Its Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) carries ₹1 lakh and its Award (Akademi Puraskar) ₹3 lakh.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Akademi Ratna carries ₹3 lakh and the Puraskar ₹1 lakh; there can be at most 40 living Fellows; in August 2026 honours went to 115 artists but the Ratna to only 7; Pasumarthi Rattaiah Sarma was among those 7 Ratna recipients.

st.3: Rouble Nagi won the Global Teacher Prize in 2026, becoming the first Indian to win it.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Ranjitsinh Disale won the Global Teacher Prize in 2020, not 2019 - so Rouble Nagi (2026) is the second Indian winner, not the first.

st.3: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith Award in 1970.

x: Only 1 is correct: the first Jnanpith (1965) went to G. Sankara Kurup. Viswanatha Satyanarayana (1970) was honoured for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu - Viswambhara is C. Narayana Reddy's; C. Narayana Reddy received it in 1988, not 1970.

st.2: Roland Garros, started in 1891, is the only Grand Slam played on clay.

x: All three statements are correct: Alexander Zverev won the French Open 2026, Roland Garros (1891) is the only Grand Slam on clay (Wimbledon is the grass one), and Heliövaara and Patten won the Wimbledon 2026 men's doubles.

st.1: Ladakh topped Phase 1 (ice events) at Leh.

x: Neither statement is correct. Haryana topped Phase 1 at Leh, with Ladakh second; the Indian Army topped Phase 2 at Gulmarg.

st.2: Mission LiFE was launched by PM Narendra Modi at COP28, Dubai.

x: Only 1 is correct: the first BRIC Summit was at Yekaterinburg in 2009. Mission LiFE was launched on 20 October 2022 at Kevadia (Ekta Nagar), not at COP28; India holds the Chairship in 2026, after Brazil (2025).

st.1: He is a historical figure revered by the Yadav community.

x: Neither statement is correct. Panduga Sayanna is revered by the Mudiraj community; his birth anniversary is 22 October and his death anniversary 10 December, not the other way round.

st.1: Its theme was '75 Years of the Constitution'.
st.4: The first animal contingent at the parade was of the Assam Rifles.

x: Only 3 is correct: the Bhairav Light Commando Battalion made its debut. The theme was '150 Years of Vande Mataram'; the Chief Guests were Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa, not Charles Michel; the first animal contingent was of the Remount and Veterinary Corps.

st.3: The NCLT was set up under the Companies Act, 2013.

x: All three statements are correct: UIDAI (2009) became statutory under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, Justice A.S. Grewal is the first NCLT President who was not an HC Chief Justice, and the NCLT was set up under the Companies Act, 2013 (not 1956).

st.4: Article 329(a) allows the High Courts to review its orders.
st.2: The last delimitation, based on the 2011 Census, was completed in 2008.

x: Only 1 is correct: the Commission was constituted in 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002. The last delimitation was based on the 2001 Census; its orders have the force of law without Parliament's approval; Article 329(a) bars courts from questioning them.

st.3: Other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President at will, without the CEC's recommendation.
st.1: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, on a notice by 50 Lok Sabha or 100 Rajya Sabha members.

x: Only 2 is correct: a three-member committee inquires into the charges. The notice needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members, not the reverse; other ECs can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation; the 2026 notices against Gyanesh Kumar were rejected, not admitted.

st.4: India has about 22 judges per 10 lakh population, against 50 recommended by the Malimath Committee (2003).
st.3: Its technology was developed by the National Informatics Centre.
st.1: India's first fully paperless district court is at Kottayam (Kerala).

x: None of the statements is correct. The first fully paperless district court is at Kalpetta, Wayanad; it was inaugurated by CJI Surya Kant, not the President; its technology came from the Kerala High Court; the norm of 50 judges per 10 lakh was the Law Commission's (1987), not the Malimath Committee's.

st.4: India is the largest steel producer, ahead of China.
st.3: The World Steel Association was established in 1967 and is headquartered in Geneva.

x: Only 1 is correct: the draft policy envisages 604 MT capacity and 45 MT exports. The NSP 2017 targeted 300 MT by 2030-31, not 2047; worldsteel is headquartered in Brussels; India is second, after China.

st.4: Phenol and acetone are produced together by the Haber process.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The facility is at Haldia, West Bengal, not Paradip; phenol and acetone are made together by the cumene process (the Haber process makes ammonia).

st.1: It is headquartered in Manila.

x: All three statements are correct: the ADB is headquartered in Manila (not Tokyo), its President is Masato Kanda, and it has lent USD 230 million for Chennai's water and sanitation.

st.4: The park size for mid-sized States is up to 25 acres.
st.2: Its portal was developed by DPIIT and its guidelines issued by NICDC.

x: Only 1 is correct: BHAVYA aims at 100 parks in six years with ₹33,660 crore. The portal is NICDC's and the guidelines DPIIT's; the NICDC-State ratio is 51:49, not 49:51; mid-sized States get 100-500 acres (25 acres is for hilly/NE States).

st.2: InvITs give market-linked returns, while infrastructure bonds pay fixed interest.

x: All three statements are correct: bank infrastructure bonds need a minimum 7-year maturity, InvITs give market-linked returns while bonds pay fixed interest, and InvITs are recognised as borrowers under SARFAESI.

st.2: Its Component II was extended to 31 March 2030.

x: Only 1 is correct: RELIEF stands for Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation. Component II was extended to 31 March 2027, not 2030; ECGC (1957) is headquartered in Mumbai, not New Delhi.

st.2: It converges 36 schemes of the Ministry of Agriculture alone.

x: Only 3 is correct: PM-DDKY is modelled on the Aspirational Districts Programme. Its nodal body is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, not NITI Aayog; it converges 36 schemes of 11 Ministries/Departments, not of one ministry.

st.1: It is a ₹84,084 crore scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

x: All three statements are correct: Samudra Manthan is a ₹84,084 crore scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (not Earth Sciences), supporting 56 exploratory and 4 stratigraphic wells, with up to 50% of drilling cost subject to ₹675 crore a well.

st.1: The UGC is a non-statutory body set up by an executive resolution.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. The UGC is a statutory body under the UGC Act, 1956; the 2023 Regulations generally require a global top-500, not top-200, ranking.

st.2: GARBH-INi is India's largest pregnancy cohort, of 12,000 women.

x: All three statements are correct: UMMID is run by the Department of Biotechnology, GARBH-INi is India's largest pregnancy cohort (12,000 women), and SEHAT ('Farm to Plate') is run jointly by ICAR and ICMR.

st.3: JJM 2.0, extended to December 2028, aims to give a Functional Household Tap Connection to all 19.36 crore urban households.

x: Only 1 is correct: Odisha ranked first in PMAY-Urban 2.0 construction. PMAY-U 2.0 was launched in September 2024, not 2025; JJM 2.0 covers the 19.36 crore rural, not urban, households.

st.1: Pralhad Joshi took additional charge of the Ministry of Education after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned; MHRD had been renamed the Ministry of Education in 2014.

x: Only 2 is correct: Justice B.V. Nagarathna succeeded Justice J.K. Maheshwari as Chairperson of the SC Legal Services Committee. MHRD was renamed the Ministry of Education in 2020, not 2014; the committee is constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, not 1995.

st.3: The employee's contribution under it is 10% of pay.

x: All three statements are correct: the UPS is a contributory scheme with an assured payout, it assures 50% of the last 12 months' average basic pay for 25 years' service, and the employee contributes 10% (the government 18.5%).

st.4: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in December 2024 and sent to a JPC.
st.1: It proposed a new Article 324A to synchronise the terms of the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies.

x: Only 3 is correct: Article 324A was proposed for municipal and panchayat polls. Synchronising Lok Sabha and Assembly terms is the proposed Article 82A; the Article 82A amendment needs no State ratification; the Bill sent to the JPC is the 129th Amendment Bill (the 131st concerns Lok Sabha seats).

st.2: Habropoda adi, a solitary bee from Arunachal reported by the Zoological Survey of India, honours the Adi tribe.

x: Only 3 is correct: Micromonospora shyamaprasadii honours Syama Prasad Mukherjee. Crotalaria phulei is named after Savitribai Phule, not Jyotirao; Habropoda adi was reported by ATREE, not the ZSI.

st.3: The National Wetland Decadal Change Atlas was prepared by NRSC, Hyderabad.
st.2: Pulicat Lake became Andhra Pradesh's Ramsar site in 2002.

x: Only 4 is correct: the National Wetland Action Plan covers 2017-2031. Gogabeel is in Bihar, not Jharkhand; AP's only Ramsar site is Kolleru Lake (2002); the Decadal Change Atlas was prepared by SAC, Ahmedabad.

st.2: Hygam and Shallbugh Wetland Conservation Reserves were designated in 2012.

x: Only 1 is correct: Hokersar and Surinsar-Mansar were designated in 2006. Hygam and Shallbugh were designated in 2022, not 2012; Wular Lake was designated in 1990, not 2002.

st.1: For cattle and buffaloes the cover is for 3 years at a premium of 6.25%.

x: Only 2 is correct: the farmer pays 15% of the premium. The 3-year cattle and buffalo premium is 6.40% (6.25% is the 3-year rate for sheep, goats and pigs); the remaining 85% is shared 60:40 in AP, a general-category State (90:10 applies to hilly and NE States).

st.3: SHRESTH benchmarks State drug regulators.

x: All three statements are correct: Dr NTR Vaidya Seva gives cashless care mainly to BPL families for 3,257 procedures, SHRESTH is the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index run by CDSCO, and it benchmarks State drug regulators, not hospitals.

st.3: Its fiscal deficit is estimated at about ₹75,868 crore.

x: All three statements are correct: the Budget was presented by Payyavula Keshav, the revenue deficit is about 1.1% of GSDP, and ₹75,868 crore is the fiscal deficit (3.84% of GSDP), not the capital expenditure.

st.1: The fiscal deficit is estimated at about 4.6% of GSDP.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. The 2026-27 fiscal deficit is about 3.8% of GSDP (4.6% is the 2025-26 revised estimate); the Budget does not assume 15% GSDP growth.

st.1: It creates new irrigation potential of 9 lakh acres and stabilises 4.3 lakh acres.

x: All three statements are correct: the hub creates new irrigation potential of 9 lakh acres and stabilises 4.3 lakh acres, the Indian School of Agriculture (with Reliance, modelled on ISB) was begun the same day, and its crops include dragon fruit, avocado and berries.

st.1: The Machilipatnam shipbuilding cluster, about ₹29,254 crore, got in-principle approval from the Centre.

x: Only 3 is correct: Kakinada SEZ was revived with MoUs of about ₹1.5 lakh crore. The ₹29,254 crore cluster is at Dugarajapatnam, not Machilipatnam; the AP Maritime Board's HQ moved from Kakinada to Amaravati, not the other way round.

st.3: It is run by Google subsidiary Raiden Infotech with Reliance Industries.

st.1: Visakhapatnam railway station received the Platinum rating, the highest level of the Green Railway Station rating of the Global Green Building Council.

x: All three statements are correct: Visakhapatnam station got the Platinum (highest, not Gold) GGBC rating, Adavi Thalli Baata targets 558 tribal roads, and Trinetra is at Naval Station Bheemunipatnam.

st.1: The Ministry of Tourism released ₹5 crore for its new building under the Museum Grant Scheme.
st.3: It holds about 5,000 palm-leaf manuscripts of the 10th–12th centuries.

x: None of the statements is correct. The ₹5 crore came from the Ministry of Culture, not Tourism; funding is 80:20, not 60:40; the about 5,000 manuscripts date from the 17th-19th centuries.

st.2: The award carries ₹3 lakh and a copper plaque.
st.1: They were announced on 26 January 2026.

x: None of the statements is correct. The awards were announced on 16 March 2026; the award carries ₹1 lakh and a copper plaque; the Telugu award went to Nandini Sidha Reddy of Telangana, not Andhra Pradesh.
